claude: Verdict basis: both deciders named F1 (llama.cpp) on documented fit under criterion 1 and said so, as the rules require. Every deciding fact I re-checked holds at source except two claims marked false in checked_facts ('one process' and Codex coverage). The default stands, on a narrower margin than either decider stated.

Material fact both deciders missed, observed in source at their own pin: llama-server's /v1/responses shim drops every non-function tool (tools/server/server-chat.cpp L274-279 at a868c3e3c5). Codex sends namespace-typed tools to a configured provider by default (openai/codex 6ece7bfc21bc: provider.rs L60-69 and L461-474, spec_plan.rs L585-590; code-search fragments show namespaced tool names for MCP, skills and multi-agent tools). Upstream issue #24295 has been open since 2026-06-08 ('Every MCP server tool ... is invisible to the model'); fix PR #23235 is a stale draft; #23229 and #25193 were closed as stale; PR #21174 was closed unmerged on 2026-09-19; PR #27751 (HTTP 400 on Codex reasoning items in multi-turn history) is also open. Codex over llama-server is therefore a known defect pending an unmerged fix, not only the 'untested path' both deciders recorded.

A finalist is stronger than the default on part of the criteria. Ollama (F2) leads criterion 7 (documented launchers for both clients, Codex's built-in provider, merged namespace, tool_search and web_search handling in openai/responses.go L842-938), criterion 6 (WSL2-aware installer with a systemd unit) and the Codex half of criterion 1. llama.cpp keeps criterion 1 only through its native Prometheus /metrics, a server with no cloud route, the fuller Anthropic surface (count_tokens, tool_choice) and unforced parallel slots, plus never being behind Ollama on the same GGUF in the two independent runs. If the coordinator counts Codex sessions with MCP tools on the local route as part of the actual workload, documented fit tips to Ollama. I keep the verdict at converged because the decision rule is documented fit, the route is optional, both deciders marked the Codex path unqualified and wrote it into their overturn checks, and Ollama lacks one stated piece outright (metrics) and has open defects of its own.

Ollama's gaps, confirmed more firmly than the deciders did: no Prometheus exporter anywhere in the tree or go.mod (not just zero-hit searches); numParallel forced to 1 for the qwen35 family, other listed architectures and all embedding models (server/sched.go L505-515); open issue #18431 (2026-09-13, confirmed by a commenter on a local 0.34.4 install), where system-role messages are hoisted into the system block and defeat the prefix cache for Claude Code started by hand. cmd/launch/claude.go L73 sets CLAUDE_CODE_TOTAL_TOKENS_REMINDER=off, which appears to avoid it (my inference). These are performance and observability defects; llama.cpp's Codex defect is a correctness defect (the tools never reach the model).

Field-wide context: every finalist has open Codex or Claude Code compatibility items (vLLM PR #56285 and issues #44576 and #57324; SGLang PR #35216 for namespace tools, still open; Ollama issues #18411, #18419 and #15912). Among the files read, only Ollama has namespace handling in merged code; vLLM was not determined.

Factual imprecision: decider 1 wrote that 'one process' can hold a chat model and an embedding model. Router mode is one router process forwarding to model instances that run as child processes. Decider 2's point that vLLM 'means two processes sharing the 24 GB card' therefore does not separate it from llama.cpp. The real difference is that llama.cpp ships the router and model lifecycle on one port, while vLLM's FAQ tells users to add their own routing layer. No upstream example shows a chat model and an embedding model in one preset; both deciders correctly marked that pairing as not run.

Overstated demerit: 'cloud features on by default' (decider 1) reads as default data egress. The FAQ says local runs send nothing (L161). What is on by default is reachability: cloudPassthroughMiddleware sits on five /v1 inference routes (routes.go L2065-2076), and cloud models and web search work until OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1. It is a one-setting hardening step, comparable to vLLM's usage-stats opt-out. Ollama's Claude Code page does use :cloud models in its examples.

The 'narrower Anthropic surface' separator is weak: Claude Code documents count_tokens as optional, a missing cache_control is 'No error', and tool_choice does not appear on the gateway protocol page. Decider 1 flagged the tool_choice dependency as not verified; it remains so.

Numbers across formats or tools: both deciders cite vLLM and SGLang figures on AWQ or FP8 weights against GGUF (same harness, different weights); both acknowledged it and neither decided on it. Decider 2 repeats ComputingForGeeks' 'half the rate on the L40S and RTX 5090', which the article supports by comparing llama-bench with Ollama's own telemetry (two tools) on cards that are not the target; on the RTX 4090 Ollama matched llama.cpp. Decider 2 also quotes the authors' pick 'for a single user ... llama.cpp', which is opinion, not evidence. The Winder Ollama arm was configured like for like; its flat 33 tok/s is specific to that model architecture.

Sibling-slot dependency: both deciders list 'SocratiCode's default embedding provider' in Ollama's favour.
